scope: current native source audit, not deployed exploit testing

findings.title: Self-asserted email grants global moderation
findings.confirmed: Registration creates an active session for an unverified email; require_moderator authorizes that email against moderator_emails. No mailbox-ownership/verified-email check is on this chain. Reports can contain private-message excerpts and moderation can remove other users content.
findings.preconditions: auth_enabled and auth_registration_enabled; configured moderator email is not already registered. Actual deployment values were not read.
findings.minimal_fix: Provision immutable account user IDs in a default-empty deployment allowlist; never derive privilege from self-asserted email or tenant-owner role. Do not auto-set email_verified.
findings.offline_test: Actual native registration with configured moderator email must receive 403 from queue and resolution, preserving reported content. Explicit trusted ID provisioning grants queue/remove to that account; another tenant owner remains denied.
findings.verification: Static native chain confirmed; isolated native reproduction/proposal is separate upcoming packet.

findings.title: Privacy refusal logs the rejected sensitive URL
findings.confirmed: Fetcher detects email/credential-like query fields, then warning logs url[:120]; redirect refusal logs current[:120]. The rejected secret/contact value is therefore eligible for operational logs even though no destination request is sent. QueryPrivacyError likewise includes rejected input repr; the runner stores/logs generic exception text.
findings.preconditions: A discovered or submitted research URL contains a sensitive value within the logged prefix, or intended field triggers QueryPrivacyError. Log reader access/forwarding is a deployment condition, not audited.
findings.minimal_fix: Log refusal kind and sanitized host only (or opaque request identifier); omit rejected input values from privacy exception messages. Do not rely on length truncation as redaction.
findings.offline_test: caplog tests for initial and redirect PII refusal assert synthetic token/email absent and outcome REFUSED_PRIVACY, no HTTP dispatch. Invalid intended field must produce value-free error/log/audit diagnostics.
findings.verification: Source-confirmed logging path; not executed, no real sensitive values read.

findings.title: No explicit no-store policy for private API responses
findings.confirmed: _secure applies browser security headers to normal and early refusals but no Cache-Control. Profile/account/result exports and social responses lack a common no-store boundary; avatar API currently explicitly allows private 24h caching.
findings.preconditions: A browser/proxy chooses to retain a private response. Actual production headers/cache exploit not tested; cookie authentication alone is not an explicit no-store response policy.
findings.minimal_fix: Request-path-aware _secure sets Cache-Control: no-store for /api and /api/*, including middleware refusals; leave non-API static paths unchanged. This intentionally overrides avatar API private caching.
findings.offline_test: Native middleware client for successful case/account/export/social, 401/404/403/429, explicit cacheable avatar/private response override; static assets retain ETag/Last-Modified/cache policy.
findings.verification: Source confirmed; narrow proposal follows separately.

findings.title: Password-reset consumption is not atomic
findings.confirmed: confirm_password_reset reads unused token, then changes password and sets used_at with ordinary ORM assignments. There is no row lock or conditional consume UPDATE. Two transactions which both read unused may both complete with last-writer password. Existing tests cover sequential reuse, not concurrent redemption.
findings.preconditions: Password recovery enabled, possession of same valid reset token, two concurrently executing requests (production PostgreSQL). Actual deployed flag and runtime race were not tested.
findings.minimal_fix: Atomically claim token in same transaction using unused/expiry predicate and rowcount/RETURNING or lock-and-recheck, then password/session updates. Exactly one transaction may redeem it.
findings.offline_test: Owned PostgreSQL two-session barrier concurrent redemption: exactly one success, one invalid-token response, single reset audit; no second surviving password/session. Sequential/expired/disabled recovery remain intact.
findings.verification: Static concurrency gap only; queued separately, no patch or runtime claim in this task.

findings.title: Complete export/delete wording exceeds actual retained record scope
findings.confirmed: Profile export says complete record and deletion removes all of it, but AuditEvent has no profile/run FK and is retained; delete_profile adds another linked audit. Job.run_id and Entitlement.profile_id have no FK and profile/run deletion does not erase them. Content reports deliberately retain subject author ID/excerpt after subject content deletion. These are explicit retention exceptions, not erased applicant/account data.
findings.preconditions: Case has audit/jobs/entitlement, or other user reports social content before its author deletes it. No unauthenticated access or over-tenant exposure is established by this finding.
findings.minimal_fix: State precise deletion and export exceptions, assign retention/erasure rules to operational jobs, minimal audits, billing linkage and moderation evidence. Cancel orphan research jobs and redact retained errors if necessary; do not blindly delete subscription accounting/security history.
findings.offline_test: Owned synthetic populated case export/delete: profile/runs/results/claims/conflicts removed; every surviving linked record enumerated with approved retention/redaction. Other-reporter report excerpt after author deletion follows disclosed retention.
findings.verification: Static relationships and product wording confirmed; retention periods/operator backups are unknown.
